assets.alt_text: The html element contains head and body; metadata belongs in head and page content in body.
assets.caption: A complete document has a root element with metadata and body content.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf diagram generated for this course; included in patch.

assets.format: SVG
assets.alt_text: Attributes refine the element, while content is nested between tags for non-void elements.
assets.caption: An element combines a tag, optional attributes, and its content; void elements do not have end tags.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf diagram generated for this course; included in patch.

assets.format: SVG
assets.alt_text: Use headings to create a meaningful content outline from larger sections to smaller ones.
assets.caption: Heading levels convey a structure that people can navigate; do not skip levels only to control appearance.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf diagram generated for this course; included in patch.

assets.format: SVG
assets.alt_text: Choose a destination that resolves correctly from the page containing the link.
assets.caption: A link href can identify a full web address, a relative resource, or an element on the current page.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf diagram generated for this course; included in patch.

assets.format: SVG
assets.alt_text: Keep every candidate valid and maintain a fallback img with appropriate alternative text.
assets.caption: The browser evaluates the candidate list and layout hint to choose a suitable image resource.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf diagram generated for this course; included in patch.

assets.format: SVG
assets.alt_text: Use th for headers, td for values, and scope or explicit relationships when needed.
assets.caption: Captions and header relationships give context to data cells beyond their visual position.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf diagram generated for this course; included in patch.

assets.format: SVG
assets.alt_text: Connect labels to controls and never treat browser validation as a security boundary.
assets.caption: Labels and native constraints help people complete a form, but the server must independently check submitted data.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf diagram generated for this course; included in patch.

assets.format: SVG
assets.alt_text: Use native elements for their intended meaning and avoid adding unnecessary landmarks.
assets.caption: Landmarks and semantic regions provide useful navigation and relationships to the document.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf diagram generated for this course; included in patch.

assets.format: SVG
assets.alt_text: Review the origin and add only the permission exceptions required by the use case.
assets.caption: An iframe loads a separate browsing context; sandbox and allow attributes limit capabilities.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf diagram generated for this course; included in patch.

assets.format: SVG
assets.alt_text: Inspect the original source and live DOM separately when debugging unexpected rendering.
assets.caption: The browser parses source markup into a document tree and loads linked resources according to their behavior.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf diagram generated for this course; included in patch.

assets.format: SVG
assets.alt_text: Avoid lazy-loading the likely largest contentful image, and do not mark every image high priority.
assets.caption: Resource priority and loading attributes are hints that should be based on the page’s real critical path.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf diagram generated for this course; included in patch.

assets.format: SVG
assets.alt_text: A clean automated report is useful evidence but does not prove the whole experience is accessible.
assets.caption: Validation is most useful as a repeated feedback loop, paired with browser and accessibility testing.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf diagram generated for this course; included in patch.

assets.format: SVG
assets.alt_text: Replace obsolete presentational choices with semantic elements and styling, then verify behavior.
assets.caption: A migration should improve meaning and usability without introducing unnecessary rewrites.
